process_area.title: Product Knowledge Mastery, Certification & Clienteling Tools

value_stream.name: Sales Enablement, Product Knowledge Mastery & Clienteling

fields.Participants: Sales Enablement, Merchandising/Category (links to VS-01), Store Ops (links to VS-07), L&D (links to VS-19.4), Product Info (links to VS-01.3), Trade Capability (links to VS-123), Master Associates

workflows.name: Product Knowledge Mastery Program & Role-Based Knowledge Standards

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-communication of "communicate expectations to associates" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-602 (ensure controlled execution — Product Knowledge Mastery, Certification & Clienteling Tools (PA-124.2).)
- operational: role-based standards; operational: maintenance cycle
Pain Points / Risks: - **Inconsistent-knowledge risk**: Associates know products unevenly; mitigated by role-based standards
- **Stale-knowledge risk**: Standards not updated for new SKUs; mitigated by maintenance cycle
System Touchpoints: - Merchandising/PIM (links to VS-01/VS-01.3); L&D/competency (links to VS-19.4/W683); enablement platform (links to W3839); apprenticeship (links to VS-123)

steps.activity: Sales Enablement/Merchandising define role-based product-knowledge mastery standards per department/role (lumber, tiles, plumbing, electrical, paint, tools, appliances, hardware; cashier, sales associate, department supervisor, Pro-Desk): the must-know product attributes, applications, compatibility, common customer jobs, and selling points

Sales Enablement/Product-Info build the knowledge base from product information (links to VS-01.3 PIM/W50, product content, specifications, SDS links to W1465), category expertise, and master-associate input, organized for quick floor reference (links to W3839)

Sales Enablement/L&D integrate the mastery standards into the competency framework (links to VS-19.4/W683/W1127) and the apprenticeship curriculum where relevant (links to VS-123/W3810), and communicate expectations to associates

fields.Participants: Sales Enablement, L&D (links to VS-19.4/W683/W1127), Store Ops (links to VS-07), Merchandising (links to VS-01), HR (links to VS-103), Master Associates

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "Sales Enablement/L&D design product-knowledge certification per role/department" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-capture of "Sales Enablement/L&D deliver certification" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - operational: practical/scenario assessment; operational: coverage analytics
Pain Points / Risks: - **Certification-without-mastery risk**: Associates pass quiz but can't apply on the floor; mitigated by practical/scenario assessment
- **Coverage-gap risk**: Stores/departments under-certified; mitigated by coverage analytics
System Touchpoints: - L&D/LMS (links to VS-19.4/W683/W1127); enablement/mobile (links to W3839); recognition (links to W630); compensation (links to VS-102); analytics (links to VS-28.1)

steps.activity: Sales Enablement/L&D design product-knowledge certification per role/department: knowledge checks (quizzes), practical demonstration (e.g., specify the right tile adhesive for a substrate, the right wire gauge for a load, tint a paint sample), and scenario-based assessment — distinct from general competency (links to VS-19.4/W683)

Sales Enablement/L&D deliver certification (via LMS/mobile links to W3839/VS-19.4), capture results (links to W683/W3841), and recognize certified associates (recognition links to W630, compensation links to VS-102 where applicable)

Sales Enablement/L&D manage periodic recertification (links to W1127 annual re-certification), remediation for not-yet-certified associates, and coverage analytics (certified % per department/store — links to W3849)

fields.Participants: Sales Enablement, Merchandising (links to VS-01), Marketing (links to VS-14), Store Ops (links to VS-07), L&D (links to VS-19.4), Store Comms (links to VS-63), Vendors
fields.Trigger: New product/category launch (links to VS-01.1); promotion (links to VS-14)

workflows.name: New-Product Launch Enablement & Rapid Knowledge Rollout

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "check completion, store coverage" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-602 (ensure controlled execution — Product Knowledge Mastery, Certification & Clienteling Tools (PA-124.2).)
- operational: rapid/mobile rollout; operational: launch enablement and sell-through tracking
Pain Points / Risks: - **Slow-rollout risk**: New product on shelf but associates unaware; mitigated by rapid/mobile rollout
- **Launch-miss risk**: Weak enablement → poor sell-through; mitigated by launch enablement and sell-through tracking
System Touchpoints: - Merchandising (links to VS-01); marketing/promo (links to VS-14); enablement/mobile (links to W3839); store comms (links to VS-63); planogram (links to VS-55); analytics (links to VS-28.1)

steps.activity: Sales Enablement/Merchandising build launch enablement for new products/categories: key features/benefits, target customer/job, differentiation, pricing/promo (links to VS-01.2/VS-14), attach opportunities, and common questions/objections — produced ahead of launch

Sales Enablement/Store-Comms roll out the knowledge rapidly to ~200 stores via mobile/micro-learning (links to W3839), store comms/tasking (links to VS-63), pre-shift huddles, and vendor training where relevant (links to W3848), timed to the launch/planogram reset (links to VS-55)
steps.r: Sales Enablement / Store Ops / Store Comms

steps.activity: Sales Enablement/Analytics verify rollout (knowledge-check completion, store coverage) and track new-product sell-through and attach (links to W3849/VS-01.1), feeding launch learning back to merchandising

fields.Participants: Sales Enablement, IT (links to VS-27/VS-113), CRM/Loyalty (links to VS-13.3), Mobile App (links to VS-75), Store Ops (links to VS-07), Data Privacy (links to VS-91), Analytics (links to VS-28.1)
fields.Trigger: Enablement-tech cycle (links to W3839); CRM maturity

workflows.name: Clienteling Tool, Customer-360 & Associate Mobile Selling Assistant

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-file of "Sales Enablement/IT deploy and operate the clienteling tool /" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-identify of "identify/recognize the customer" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-measure of "measure clienteling effectiveness" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-602 (ensure controlled execution — Product Knowledge Mastery, Certification & Clienteling Tools (PA-124.2).)
- operational: adoption tracking and coaching; operational: RA 10173 governance (links to VS-91)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Adoption-gap risk**: Tool deployed but associates don't use it; mitigated by adoption tracking and coaching
- **Privacy risk**: Customer-360 mishandled; mitigated by RA 10173 governance (links to VS-91)
System Touchpoints: - CRM/loyalty (links to VS-13.3); mobile (links to VS-75); enterprise architecture (links to VS-113); data privacy (links to VS-91); POS (links to VS-08); project/quote (links to VS-66/VS-11); analytics (links to VS-28.1)

steps.activity: Sales Enablement/IT deploy and operate the clienteling tool / associate mobile selling assistant: a single customer view (profile, purchase history, loyalty tier/points, project/quote history links to VS-66/VS-11, preferences, last interactions) available to the associate at the point of sale, sourced from CRM/loyalty (links to VS-13.3) — enabling recognition, relevant recommendations, and follow-up

Sales Enablement/Store-Ops drive clienteling adoption: identify/recognize the customer (loyalty lookup, mobile number), use the customer-360 to personalize (recall last project, suggest replenishment/next-step), capture notes/tasks, and trigger follow-up (links to VS-13/W3845) — with RA 10173-compliant data handling (links to VS-91)

Sales Enablement/Analytics measure clienteling effectiveness (customer-identification rate, repeat/attach uplift for identified customers, associate adoption — links to W3849) and improve the tool and practice

fields.Participants: Sales Enablement, Loyalty/CRM (links to VS-13.2), Store Ops (links to VS-07), POS (links to VS-08), Marketing (links to VS-14), L&D (links to VS-19.4), Trade Pro (links to VS-43)
fields.Trigger: Loyalty strategy (links to VS-13); enablement cycle

workflows.name: Loyalty, Identification & Enrollment Enablement at Point of Sale

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-identify of "identify customers and enroll loyalty members at POS" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-track of "track identification rate, enrollment conversion, and loyalty-driven…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-602 (ensure controlled execution — Product Knowledge Mastery, Certification & Clienteling Tools (PA-124.2).)
- operational: identification enablement; operational: POS/streamlined process
Pain Points / Risks: - **Low-identification risk**: Customers transact unidentified, losing the customer-360 and loyalty value; mitigated by identification enablement
- **Enrollment-friction risk**: Enrollment process too slow; mitigated by POS/streamlined process
System Touchpoints: - Loyalty/CRM (links to VS-13.2); POS (links to VS-08); trade pro (links to VS-43); enablement/mobile (links to W3839); analytics (links to VS-28.1)

steps.activity: Sales Enablement/Loyalty build the enablement to identify customers and enroll loyalty members at POS: scripts/prompts, value props for enrollment, trade-pro identification (links to VS-43), and use of the customer-360 (links to W3844) — translating the loyalty program (links to VS-13.2) into associate behavior
Sales Enablement/Store-Ops coach and reinforce identification/enrollment behavior on the floor, and address friction (slow POS lookup, weak value prop) with Loyalty/IT (links to VS-13/VS-08)
Sales Enablement/Analytics track identification rate, enrollment conversion, and loyalty-driven attach/basket uplift (links to W3849/VS-13.2), and report to commercial/loyalty governance

fields.Participants: Sales Enablement, In-Store Services (links to VS-09), Installation (links to VS-12), Delivery (links to VS-06/VS-56), Warranty (links to VS-53), Project/Design (links to VS-66), Store Ops (links to VS-07), L&D (links to VS-19.4)
fields.Trigger: Service strategy (links to VS-09/VS-12); enablement cycle

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-measure of "measure service/add-on attach rate and revenue contribution per category/store" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-602 (ensure controlled execution — Product Knowledge Mastery, Certification & Clienteling Tools (PA-124.2).)
- operational: attach enablement; operational: standard triggers and estimation (links to VS-09)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Service-under-attach risk**: Services available but rarely attached; mitigated by attach enablement
- **Inconsistent-quote risk**: Service attach quoted inconsistently; mitigated by standard triggers and estimation (links to VS-09.2)
System Touchpoints: - In-store services (links to VS-09); installation (links to VS-12); delivery (links to VS-06/VS-56); warranty (links to VS-53); project/design (links to VS-66); analytics (links to VS-28.1)

steps.activity: Sales Enablement/In-Store-Services build enablement to sell and attach services/add-ons: fabrication (cut/thread — links to VS-09.1), paint tinting (links to W898), estimation (links to VS-09.2), installation (links to VS-12), delivery (links to VS-06/VS-56), extended warranty/protection (links to VS-53.3), and project/design consultation (links to VS-66) — when and how to surface each

Sales Enablement/Store-Ops coach associates on service/add-on attach triggers (e.g., appliance → installation + delivery + protection; paint → tinting + supplies; large project → estimation + design + delivery), and integrate into category playbooks (links to W3835)
Sales Enablement/Analytics measure service/add-on attach rate and revenue contribution per category/store (links to W3849/VS-09/VS-12), and prioritize high-value attach opportunities

fields.Participants: Sales Enablement, Insights (links to VS-44), Store Ops (links to VS-07), L&D (links to VS-19.4), CX (links to VS-13), Compliance (links to VS-22), Mystery Shopping vendor

workflows.name: Selling Quality Assurance, Mystery Shopping & Customer Interaction Audit

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-capture of "Sales Enablement/Insights design the selling-quality program" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System continuous audit of "audits, score stores/associates, and feed findings into coaching" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-post of "posture to commercial/store leadership" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: varied scenarios and multiple signals; operational: coaching linkage
Pain Points / Risks: - **Measurement-gaming risk**: Associates behave only when shopped; mitigated by varied scenarios and multiple signals
- **Feedback-loop risk**: Findings not acted on; mitigated by coaching linkage
System Touchpoints: - Insights/mystery shopping (links to VS-44); CX (links to VS-13); call center (links to VS-13.1); analytics (links to VS-28.1); store ops (links to VS-07)

steps.activity: Sales Enablement/Insights design the selling-quality program: mystery shopping (scenario-based visits per store/department), customer-interaction audits (POS transaction review, recorded-call review for call center links to VS-13.1), and a quality rubric (greeting, needs-discovery, product knowledge, attach, loyalty, closing)
Sales Enablement/Store-Ops execute mystery shopping/audits, score stores/associates, and feed findings into coaching (links to W3836), recognition (links to W3838), and corrective action
Sales Enablement/Insights correlate selling-quality scores with selling KPIs (basket, attach, conversion, CSAT — links to W3849/VS-13) and report quality posture to commercial/store leadership

fields.Participants: Sales Enablement, Merchandising (links to VS-01), Vendor Mgmt (links to VS-03), Retail Media (links to VS-48), L&D (links to VS-19.4), Compliance/ABC (links to VS-86.3), Legal (links to VS-100.3)

workflows.name: Product Knowledge Content & Vendor Training Governance

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "Sales Enablement/Vendor-Mgmt govern vendor-led training and vendor-funded content" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "report to merchandising/vendor scorecard" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: brand-neutrality and balanced content; operational: PIM linkage and content governance
Pain Points / Risks: - **Vendor-bias risk**: Vendor content skews associate selling; mitigated by brand-neutrality and balanced content
- **Accuracy risk**: Outdated/incorrect product content; mitigated by PIM linkage and content governance
System Touchpoints: - Merchandising/PIM (links to VS-01/VS-01.3); vendor (links to VS-03); retail media (links to VS-48); ABC (links to VS-86.3); legal (links to VS-100.3); vendor scorecard (links to VS-67)

steps.activity: Sales Enablement/Merchandising manage the product-knowledge content portfolio: BuildRight-authored content (links to W3841), vendor-supplied product content, and retail-media-aligned content (links to VS-48), ensuring accuracy and consistency with PIM (links to VS-01.3)

Sales Enablement/Vendor-Mgmt govern vendor-led training and vendor-funded content: compliant with ABC (links to VS-86.3), brand-neutral (no improper brand preference — links to W3824), contractually documented (links to W688), and balanced across the assortment
Sales Enablement/Analytics measure content/vendor-training effectiveness and knowledge outcomes (links to W3842/W3849), and report to merchandising/vendor scorecard (links to VS-67)
